title: Typing Warriors
tagline: Type against players and bots, with an ELO rating for every keyboard layout.
summary: Typing Warriors is a typing duel for one to six players, with bots from beginner to champion. Five modes play differently: a race through one text, a last-one-typing round with less time every wave, a table of words that everybody grabs from (some with power-ups), a 60-second sprint with a combo, and Switch Wars, where the text must be typed with two keyboard layouts in turn.

You choose your keyboard layout, and a helper keyboard shows it: QWERTZ, QWERTY, AZERTY, Dvorak, Colemak, Colemak-DH, Workman, Norman, Bépo, and the Neo family (Neo 2, NeoQwertz, Bone, Mine, Noted, AdNW, KOY, 3l). Your rating counts per layout, so a Neo beginner is not measured by the QWERTZ veteran they also are.

A course teaches every layout step by step, the home row first, with stars for accuracy and speed. The switch trainer practises changing between two layouts: the game sees from your key presses which layout is active wherever the two differ, and says so.
players: 1-6 (against bots, or online in one room)

controls.action: Type what is shown. A wrong key counts as a typo; the cursor waits for the right one
Word Loot: let go of the word you are typing. Course: Esc leaves the lesson
After a lesson: the next one
Switch Wars and the switch trainer: change the layout when the text changes colour
Tap the text to bring up the phone's keyboard; "Keyboard" shows or hides the helper keyboard

caveat: Typing Warriors is made by an AI (Claude): its rules, its word lists and its code. The keyboard layouts come from xkeyboard-config and the Neo project. So far it was played by its maker and by bots only; the bots' speeds and the rating steps are first guesses.
